item.text:
**4B.8 Research Note: Srettha Thavisin in 2024**

**Bottom line:** mixed, leaning positive on constitutional transfer of power, but weaker on coalition discipline and constitutional propriety. I found clear evidence that his removal and replacement followed constitutional channels. I also found evidence that the dismissal was triggered by his ethically controversial cabinet appointment and that his coalition was vulnerable to a shakeup.

- **Thai court to decide embattled PM Srettha’s fate on August 14**  
  **Publisher:** Reuters via ThePrint  
  **Date:** July 24, 2024  
  **URL:** https://theprint.in/world/thai-court-to-decide-embattled-pm-sretthas-fate-on-august-14/2188597/  
  **Claim:** Reuters reported that the case against Srettha stemmed from his appointment of Pichit Chuenban, and that if removed, parliament would elect a new premier. This supports a constitutional, rather than extra-constitutional, succession path, but it also shows his appointment choice had triggered a formal constitutional challenge.  
  **QIDs:** 4B.8, 4B.5

- **Thai politics braces for shakeup after court dismisses PM Srettha Thavisin**  
  **Publisher:** Reuters via Investing.com  
  **Date:** August 13-14, 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/judgment-day-for-thai-pm-srettha-as-court-rules-on-dismissal-case-3570233  
  **Claim:** Reuters said Srettha’s dismissal could require parliament to elect a new premier and potentially reshape the governing alliance. That is evidence that succession still ran through constitutional institutions, but also that his coalition was fragile and the ruling alliance was unstable.  
  **QIDs:** 4B.8, 4B.5

- **Thai court removes Srettha Thavisin as prime minister after less than a year**  
  **Publisher:** Reuters via The Guardian  
  **Date:** August 14, 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.theguardian.com/world/article/2024/aug/14/thailand-pm-srettha-thavisin-court-case-dismissal-ruling-judgment  
  **Claim:** Reuters reported that the Constitutional Court dismissed Srettha for appointing a former lawyer who had served jail time, and that this raised the prospect of political upheaval and a reset of the governing alliance. This is negative evidence on constitutional propriety and coalition discipline.  
  **QIDs:** 4B.8, 4B.5

- **Thai king endorses Paetongtarn Shinawatra as prime minister**  
  **Publisher:** Reuters via Investing.com  
  **Date:** August 18, 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/thai-king-endorses-paetongtarn-shinawatra-as-prime-minister-3576565  
  **Claim:** Reuters reported that parliament elected Paetongtarn two days after Srettha’s dismissal and the king then endorsed her, showing an orderly constitutional transfer of power after his removal. That is the strongest positive evidence for respecting constitutional succession rules.  
  **QIDs:** 4B.8, 4B.1

- **Thailand’s king swears in new government after turmoil**  
  **Publisher:** Reuters via Investing.com  
  **Date:** September 6, 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/thailands-king-swears-in-new-government-after-turmoil-3605387  
  **Claim:** Reuters reported that Paetongtarn and her cabinet were sworn in after Srettha’s court removal, confirming that the transfer of executive authority remained inside constitutional channels.  
  **QIDs:** 4B.8, 4B.1

- **Pheu Thai digital wallet project endorsed by all coalition partners**  
  **Publisher:** Thai Newsroom  
  **Date:** April 23, 2024  
  **URL:** https://thainewsroom.com/2024/04/23/pheu-thai-digital-wallet-project-endorsed-by-all-coalition-partners/  
  **Claim:** The report says all coalition partners publicly backed Srettha’s flagship digital-wallet project. This is only weak, indirect evidence of coalition coordination, but it is the clearest 2024 sign I found that his government was still managing coalition commitments publicly.  
  **QIDs:** 4B.8, 4B.2

**Search gap**
- I did not find strong direct evidence about term limits, because Thailand’s 2024 Srettha record does not turn on a term-limit issue.
- I also did not find a clean primary source showing a written coalition pact being honored or broken by Srettha beyond public support for the digital-wallet program and the later alliance shakeup after his dismissal.
